record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For every tetracyclic graph G on n >= 26 vertices, is the energy E(G) at most E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}), where P_n^{6,6;6,6} is the graph formed from four copies of C_6 and a path P_(n-24) by joining two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and the other two 6-cycles to the other endpoint, one edge per attachment? Must equality occur only for G isomorphic to P_n^{6,6;6,6}?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the quadricyclic (also called tetracyclic) graphs maximizing the energy remains open.
Conjecture 5.12 Let G be a tetracyclic graph on n vertices with n >= 26. Then E(G) <= E(P6,6;6,6_n) with equality if and only if G ≡ P6,6;6,6_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The energy of a finite simple graph G is defined as E(G) = sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. A connected graph on n vertices is called tetracyclic (or quadricyclic) if it has exactly n+3 edges, i.e., its cyclomatic number is 4.

For n ≥ 26, let P_n^{6,6;6,6} denote the graph constructed as follows: take four disjoint copies of the 6-cycle C_6 and a path P_{n-24} on n-24 vertices; designate two of the C_6's and attach each of them to one endpoint of the path by adding a single edge from a vertex of the cycle to that endpoint; attach the other two C_6's similarly to the other endpoint of the path by single edges. The resulting connected graph has n vertices and is tetracyclic.

Prove or disprove: For every tetracyclic graph G on n ≥ 26 vertices,
   E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}),
with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to P_n^{6,6;6,6}.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches indicate that the problem of identifying the tetracyclic (quadricyclic) graph of maximum energy is still considered open. The analogous conjectures for unicyclic and bipartite bicyclic graphs have been resolved, while extremal maximum-energy problems for tricyclic and tetracyclic graphs are repeatedly listed as unresolved in surveys on graph energy. No source confirming a complete proof of the specific conjecture for n ≥ 26 with extremal graph P_n^{6,6;6,6} was located.

status_evidence.title: Graphs Extremal with Regard to Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of extremal energy results indicating tricyclic and tetracyclic maximum-energy problems are not fully resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The tetracyclic maximum-energy problem is listed as an open extremal problem.

status_evidence.title: Complete solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the unicyclic case; tetracyclic case not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Only the unicyclic analogue has been completely solved by these methods.

status_evidence.title: Energy of Graphs – open problems (Stevanović)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on extremal graph energy.
status_evidence.claim: Maximum-energy extremal problems for higher cyclomatic classes remain open.
